title: Representative compatibility of strict-local coefficient and symmetry transport
statement: Let Λ, f:X→Y, s:Spec Ω→Y, F, ρ, A, B, g, h, σ be as in [def-weil-pbc-strict-local-module-sections-set-equiv]. For each affine pointed etale neighbourhood j of s [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit] and section z of F on X×_Y V_j, send z along the module inverse-image unit for g, restrict along the terminal-to-iterated-pullback map induced by σ followed by the strict-henselization base-change leg, and identify terminal sections with Γ(A,g*F). The explicit equivalence [def-weil-pbc-strict-local-module-sections-set-equiv] sends this section to the set inverse-image unit for h followed by restriction along strictHenselizationSectionMap f s j. This is an identity for any f, with no qcqs assumption, and does not assert bijectivity of a stalk map.

proof.text: Expand the explicit equivalence. The global-section/terminal-section isomorphism cancels the inverse terminal-section identification at the end of the module restriction map.

The coefficient comparison is the adjoint transpose of the forgotten module unit. Apply the homEquiv unit identity and the inverse comparison to identify the forgotten module unit with the set unit. Naturality of this inverse comparison moves it past restriction to the terminal object.

Use the unit equation of the inverse-image composition comparison for h and σ. Since σ≫h=g, inverse composition sends the g-unit to the iterated h-unit and σ-unit, with the canonical fibre-product pasting isomorphism. Naturality moves this identity past restriction.

The inverse-image/restriction comparison for the etale isomorphism σ sends the σ-unit to restriction along the fibre-product projection. Compose with the inverse map at the terminal isomorphism over B. The resulting morphism to the iterated pullback is strictHenselizationSectionMap: compare both scheme projections using pullback.lift_fst, pullback.lift_snd, pullbackSymmetry_hom_comp_snd and the pullback pasting projections. Functoriality of restriction proves the displayed representative identity. No argument uses nonzero coefficients, nonempty X, or qcqs.
